first.rationale: Competitive entry pricing is directly taking price-sensitive SMB accounts, and prior evidence indicates targeted promotional pricing can restore acquisition and revenue. Because the primary objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue, verify the archived pricing experiment for retention, cohort quality, discount durability, and payback evidence before committing; absent strong downstream evidence, keep the test narrowly targeted and guarded.

final.rationale: Reject promotional pricing because the verified source shows a 12% decline in 30-day retention despite acquisition and revenue lift, conflicting with sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Run an onboarding simplification experiment instead: completion is down 4%, activation is down 6%, and prior evidence links shorter onboarding and fewer signup requirements to faster time-to-value, stronger adoption, and durable first-week activation. Use a controlled experiment with qualified-revenue and retention guardrails rather than assuming prior gains will fully replicate.
